chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you fear a discord between the two, then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.'
He said: 'The two judges stipulate; if they wish, they separate them, and if they wish, they gather them. So whether they separate or gather, it is valid.'

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِح: The pious servant (title of the 7th Imam, Musa al-Kazim)
key_terms.حَكَم: Judge or arbitrator appointed to resolve disputes

ai.seo_question: What is the legal authority of the two judges appointed to resolve marital discord in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the two appointed arbiters (hukkam) possess the discretionary authority to either effect a divorce or reconcile the couple, with both outcomes being legally binding. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the arbiters' decision is not merely advisory but constitutes a decisive judicial ruling, reflecting the practical application of Quran 4:35 in resolving marital discord through impartial mediation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Al Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:35] And if you fear a discord between the two, then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The two judges stipulate (specify) that if they so desire to they would separate them, and if they so desire to they would gather them. So, whether they separate or gather, it is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “

I once asked the virtuous servant of Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘If you are afraid of discord between them then send one arbitrator from his people and another from her people.’ [4:35]

He (the Imam) then said, ‘The two arbitrators stipulate upon them that their decision to separate or bring them together must be treated binding and on that basis if they separate or bring them together it is permissible.’”
